title: Microsoft Teams: unified agent and app installation management across the Teams and Microsoft 365 admin centres
summary: The roadmap facts, administrative roles, controls and PowerShell parameters are supported. Remove the unsupported assurance that unification cannot change data access or agent permissions; minor corrections concern licensing context, an abbreviated availability path and a checklist control missing from the table.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans installation changes made in either admin centre to be enforced across Teams, Outlook and Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: Administrators using the Microsoft 365 admin center and Teams admin center will be able to apply app and agent installation changes once and have them consistently enforced across Teams, Outlook, and Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: The roadmap states that Microsoft 365 admin centre installation changes previously applied only to Outlook and Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Previously, installation changes made in the Microsoft 365 admin center only applied to Outlook and Microsoft 365

claims.claim: The roadmap states that Teams admin centre installation changes previously applied only to Teams.
claims.quote: while changes made in the Teams admin center only applied to Teams.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block controls the app's organisation-wide blocked state.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps. 2. Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: The Teams PowerShell module documents Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked <Boolean> for changing app state.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true

claims.claim: The printed Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Users and groups > Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization > Availability > Edit availability > Available to path reaches app availability.
claims.quote: Select the Users and groups tab. 4. Under Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization, select Availability. 5. Select Edit availability. 6. Select the required option from Available to menu.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -AppAssignmentType Everyone sets app availability to Everyone.
claims.quote: Updates the availability value for Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b) to Everyone.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Integrated Apps > Available Apps > app > Edit Users reaches the cross-application app availability control.
claims.quote: Scroll down and select Edit Users or select the Users tab in the overview pane. Read more about user groups and assignments earlier in this article. 6. Select the availability status of the app you want to set:
claims.fix: The path stops on the right pane but before the availability selection. Use 'Settings > Integrated Apps > Available Apps > app > Edit Users > availability status', with 'availability status' as the placeholder for 'No users in the organization can install', 'All users in the organization can install', or 'Specific users/group in the organization can install'.

claims.claim: A dedicated automation operation for the pre-unification Integrated apps availability control is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Integrated apps availability Edit users Microsoft Graph beta app management API PowerShell; "Integrated apps" "Graph" "availability". Read teams-apps-work-on-outlook-and-m365, Update-M365TeamsApp and Graph beta teamsApp; no matching pre-unification operation found.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Move to unified app management starts tenant unification.
claims.quote: Go to Teams apps > Manage apps. 2. Select Move to unified app management. A dialog box appears to ask for your consent to move to the unified agent and app management experience.

claims.claim: An API or PowerShell operation for moving the tenant to unified app management is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Move to unified app management" PowerShell API migration; "unified app management" "migration" "PowerShell"; "Move to unified app management" "API". Read uam-tac-mac and app-centric-management; results give portal consent steps, not an operation for this move.

claims.quote: After your tenant is unified, all changes to org-wide settings, agent app, status, or availability in TAC are automatically synchronized in MAC and vice versa.

claims.claim: Learn says tenants that never modified org-wide defaults, app availability or block/unblock settings in either centre are automatically unified.
claims.quote: If your tenant never modified its org-wide defaults, app availability, or app block or unblock settings in either TAC or MAC, then your tenant's app availability policies are automatically unified.

claims.claim: Learn documents Move to unified app management as the route for tenants with previously modified settings.
claims.quote: If your tenant has custom app changes but no differences in app availability: 1. Go to Teams apps > Manage apps. 2. Select Move to unified app management.

claims.claim: The unification flow separately lets administrators align org-wide default settings.
claims.quote: The Align org-wide app settings page appears. Here you can select the org-wide default settings that you want to apply across TAC and MAC.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Administrators can select which centre's app status and availability settings to apply for an individual app with differences.
claims.quote: Select any individual app and review the App status and Availability. Go to Review settings for the selected app to check the App status and Availability. Select the admin center’s settings that you want to apply from the Apply settings from drop-down list and select Apply settings.

claims.claim: App availability differences can also be resolved in bulk using either centre's settings.
claims.quote: Select multiple apps at a time and select either Teams admin center or Microsoft 365 admin center from the Apply settings from drop-down list.

claims.claim: The alignment page offers a CSV download of app status and availability settings.
claims.quote: Select the Excel icon in the top-right corner to download the App status and Availability settings as a CSV file.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: The cross-application app documentation describes an app blocked in Teams remaining downloadable and usable in Outlook and the Microsoft Copilot application.
claims.quote: If you had previously blocked the Foo app on the Teams admin center | Users in your organization can't download and use Foo on Teams. | Users in your organization can download and use Foo in the Microsoft Copilot application.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises keeping blocked apps and org-wide app settings synchronized between centres until migration to prevent disruptions.
claims.quote: Until your tenant is migrated to unified app management, ensure that the settings in both admin centers, such as blocked apps or org-wide app settings, remain synchronized. This measure prevents unexpected disruptions or issues with agent and app functionality.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Unification does not change what an app reads or its agent permissions.
claims.quote: Searched: unified app management agent permissions data access unchanged; "unified agent and app management" "permissions". Read uam-tac-mac, manage-apps and app-centric-management; none states this assurance for cross-centre unification.
claims.fix: Replace 'Unification changes where an app or agent can be installed, not what it reads.' with 'The roadmap describes a change to where app and agent installation changes are enforced.' Replace 'Agent permissions are unchanged by anything the sources describe, so existing controls for each agent still apply.' with 'Confirm each agent's data permissions and action permissions separately before changing its availability.' The retained-consent passage in app-centric-management concerns a different migration and does not establish this claim.

claims.claim: The unified-management page describes availability and installation management rather than detailing agents' post-installation actions.
claims.quote: Unified agent and app management helps you unify agents, apps availability across Teams admin center (TAC) and Microsoft 365 admin center (MAC).

claims.quote: With unified agent app management, you can now manage agents and apps via the Teams admin center or Integrated apps page in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Any changes made in either admin center are automatically synchronized.
